name: Botswana
summary: A will can dispose of the whole estate: the Wills Act (Cap. 31:04) sets formalities, not reserved shares. A separate Act gives the surviving spouse and family a claim to provision, but not for estates run under customary law. Trusts exist under common law; no private foundation law was found.
family_claims: Succession (Rights of the Surviving Spouse and Inheritance Family Provisions) Act, Cap. 31:03, provides family provision; its s. 3 excludes estates administered under customary law. Details of the claim were not retrieved.
foreign_law_note: No source on whether a resident foreigner can choose their national law. Customary law applies to many Batswana estates.
trust_note: Trusts are recognised under common law and the Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 31:01) deals with property given in trust; no dedicated trust statute was found. No private-foundation law was found.
open_questions: Content and thresholds of Cap. 31:03 not read.
Botswana trust statute (if any) and foundations not found; both answers provisional.
Conflict rule for foreigners' succession not found.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
